input.productDescription: Documentation homepage for a payments API that software developers integrate into their products. It lets a developer find the right starting point quickly: a quickstart with a copyable code sample, guides by use case (accept a payment, subscriptions, payouts, refunds, webhooks), the API reference, client libraries for several languages, and the changelog and system status. Developers visit it many times a day while in the middle of a task.
audience: Software developers integrating payments into their products
Engineers on call checking API status or recent changes
primaryTasks: Copy a working quickstart code sample
Find a guide for a specific use case
Jump to an API reference endpoint
Pick and install a client library for a language
Check the changelog and system status
avoid: Marketing-style hero with abstract blobs or gradients
Decorative motion that slows repeated use
Low-contrast grey-on-grey code and body text
constraints: Vite + React + plain CSS only, no UI kits or Tailwind
Single responsive page for phones and desktops
Developers return many times a day, so scanning speed and keyboard access matter more than first-visit persuasion

evidence.summary: npm install in a clean directory holding only package.json: exit 0, no warning or error lines, 0 vulnerabilities.
npm run build (Vite 8.3.4, 62 modules): exit 0, no warning lines. CSS 38 kB (7 kB gzip), JS 274 kB (85 kB gzip), five Plex font files.

TypeScript 7.0.2 tsc --checkJs over src/, non-strict, config kept outside the project: exit 0, 0 errors. Strict mode, recorded for information only, reports 26 errors that are all inference limits of unannotated JavaScript.
ESLint 9 with eslint-plugin-react-hooks 7 (compiler-era rules such as set-state-in-effect, refs, purity) and react-refresh, out-of-tree config: 35 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings.

Vite dev server (where React development-only warnings appear) exercised through all language tabs, copy, headers disclosure, search flow, filter, theme toggle, phone-width menu and a ?lang=#id deep link: no console warnings or errors.

27 viewport widths from 320 to 2560 px in light and dark: documentElement.scrollWidth never exceeds the viewport, no element sits off-screen (outside intentional code scrollers), no text is clipped by overflow.
Zoom equivalents 640 px (200%) and 426 px (300%): no overflow. Browser default font size set to 32 px in a 1280 px window: no overflow, layout switches to the compact nav by itself (rem breakpoints).

DOM integrity: 99 unique IDs, 0 in-page links that point nowhere, 0 broken aria-labelledby or aria-controls references, 0 external hrefs, 0 img/picture/video/canvas elements, 1 h1, all buttons named, skip link off-screen when unfocused, page requests only its own origin, CLS 0.01.

Non-text contrast computed from values read off the rendered page in both themes: panel border 1.59 / 1.67:1 vs canvas, row divider 1.41 / 1.45:1, control borders 3.11 to 5.73:1, focus ring 16.2 to 17.9:1, status bars 3.86 to 7.23:1.
Source audit: no literal colour values outside src/styles/tokens.css; no literal px values other than the 1px visually-hidden clip; 618 var(--) references in component CSS.

design.md: direction and rejected alternatives, token overrides and adaptations, structure, eight design principles with decisions and checks, seven UX principles with evidence labels, UI states, assumptions, verification summary and remaining risks.
